highlights.title: How to Run a Chatbot on Your Own Computer
highlights.summary: Installing a large language model on your personal computer gives you a handy digital assistant that won’t compromise your data privacy.
body: It's no exaggeration to say the large language models that power AI bots like ChatGPT and Gemini are changing the world. Many of us are now relying on them for coding, writing, summarizing, and searching the web. Whatever directions AI goes in over the next few years, LLMs will be part of that future.

If you use ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, or any of the other AI platforms, then you're using an LLM. What's less commonly known is that these LLMs can be run locally, on your own computer. The key benefits are offline access and greater privacy, because you're not sending anything to the cloud for anyone else to analyze or review.

You're also not paying any AI companies a monthly subscription or hitting any usage rates. Numerous LLMs are available to download for free, including from big names like Meta and Google. Though they tend not to be as advanced or as speedy as the LLMs inside the apps you have to pay for, they're capable enough for everyday use, and you can pick and choose between them as needed.

Opoku netted for the second time following his summer move from Belgian outfit Zulte Waragem, while Eom - the architect of that opener - then got on the scoresheet himself just before half-time with only his second league goal since November. The routine victory meant Vitor Matos' men have collected seven points from a possible nine, while out-of-sorts Derby are still waiting for their first win of the new campaign.

Earlier, Ryan Hedges had the ball in the net for the hosts after just 18 seconds, but that was the nearest John Eustace's men would get to the Swansea goal during a sluggish opening half-hour in which they did not muster a single shot that counted.

highlights.title: Pokémon TCG Pocket adds a game-changing new kind of card this October
highlights.summary: During a Pokémon TCG Pocket panel at the PokémonXP event in San Francisco, The Pokémon Company teased some exciting new types of cards for the mobile game. Namely, dual-type cards will make their way to the popular mobile game soon.
body: Dual-type cards will become a thing in Pokémon TCG Pocket starting in October. The first dual-type card to arrive will be Mega Mewtwo X ex, which is a Psychic/Fighting-type Pokémon. It has 180 HP and a 100+ power Dual Impact ability that reads "If a stadium is in play, this attack does 40 more damage." This was highlighted in the latest trailer for Pokémon TCG Pocket, which also confirmed that ex cards for partner Pokémon Piplup and Fuecoco would arrive in October.

Dual-type Pokémon have been a thing in the video games ever since the first generation, but didn't come to the physical Pokémon Trading Card Game until the mid-2000s. According to Bulbapedia, there have been at least 90 dual-type Pokémon cards released in the decades since.

That made the fact that they were missing from Pokémon TCG Pocket a bit surprising initially, although the digital card game certainly hasn't suffered from a shortage of cards for players to collect. While Mega Mewtwo X ex is the only confirmed dual-type card for Pokémon TCG Pocket right now, a blog post on the Pokémon website confirms that more will follow.

highlights.title: Nvidia’s AI advantage is moving beyond the GPU
highlights.summary: The new generation of data center systems is increasing efficiency with smarter traffic control instead of just more processor cycles.
body: Before this week, the dominant story about Nvidia went something like this: For the first few years of the AI boom, Nvidia was the only source for state-of-the-art GPUs, which became immensely profitable as the industry scaled out. In the last few years, hyperscalers like Amazon and Google have started building their own chips, and Nvidia is no longer the only game in town, leading many investors to wonder how durable its advantage really is.

It’s a compelling story, and mostly true. After growing its market cap 10x between the start of 2023 and mid-2025, Nvidia shares have been on a more modest trajectory for the past year, driven by concerns about GPU competition.

A new narrative has taken shape since the company’s earnings on Wednesday and investors are starting to realize that Nvidia’s advantage goes far beyond GPUs. As AI’s compute grows into the gigawatt scale, orchestration has become an increasingly complex task. Not surprisingly, Nvidia has built much of the state-of-the-art hardware needed to handle it, giving the company a huge advantage in the systems that surround the GPU even as it sees increased competition on the GPUs themselves.
points: The new generation of data center systems is increasing efficiency with smarter traffic control instead of just more processor cycles.

highlights.title: ‘It gives Shein’: how did polyester become the world’s most-hated material?
highlights.summary: Due to its ubiquity in fast fashion, gen Z are pushing back against the synthetic material and using it as an insult. In 2015, Kate Moss called an easyJet pilot a “basic bitch” and a catchy new insult meaning obvious and uncool hit the mainstream.
body: But its use as a figurative insult also echoes a literal backlash against polyester, now the most-produced synthetic fibre on the planet.

In gyms, the pilates princess aesthetic with its synthetic matching sets is waning while 1990s-style exercise gear is becoming fashionable once more as many lionize exercise garments displaying visible sweat – think Sylvester Stallone in Rocky, or John Travolta being sweatily hypnotized by Jamie Lee Curtis’s rocking pelvis in the 1985 movie Perfect.

Some of the pushback centres around polyester’s impact on the planet. Derived from fossil fuels, it does not biodegrade, and sheds microplastics when washed. Many anti-polyester influencers, however, talk about giving up the fabric in the same way they might talk about giving up sugar, sharing content with hashtags such as #naturalfibers, #antipolyester and #nontoxicclothing while posting videos of large shopping hauls of cotton and linen from Zara.

highlights.title: The Galaxy Z Flip 8 is at its best when there’s friction
highlights.summary: What do you want from a flip phone when it's closed? A simple interface, perhaps notifications and a widget or two, for handling the basics? Or a fully fledged Android experience shrunk down for the Flip form factor?
body: The cover screen feels more like a phone than ever, but the limitations are still what makes it.
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Although the Z Flip 8’s hardware is almost unchanged year-on-year, Samsung has fundamentally rethought how this phone is meant to be used when shut. The cover screen feels more like a regular Android phone, with easier access to the full versions of every single app, letting you browse social media, watch movies, and play games without ever opening the phone. Not every app works well on a tiny square screen with two cameras in the middle of it, but even when they don’t, that friction between me and the distractions of my phone still feels as much a feature as a bug.

Everything exciting about the Z Flip 8 lies in its 4-inch cover screen, which is now more versatile than ever thanks to a homescreen redesign. Swiping down from the top left now brings up your notifications, while swiping from the top right instead shows a cover-screen-optimized version of the Quick Settings panel. Immediately, this feels more like a phone.

highlights.title: Trump’s EPA wants to let data centers hide their air pollution
highlights.summary: Just as new data centers face growing backlash from neighboring communities, the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is about to make it harder for people to weigh in on any pollution those centers create.
body: The Trump administration wants to scrap another federal air pollution rule. Advocates say it’ll help data center developers avoid public scrutiny.

The EPA plans to toss out a federal rule requiring public notice and an opportunity to comment when certain industrial sites apply for an air permit. Advocates warn that the move would allow data center developers and other industries to break ground without giving nearby residents a say, or even a warning that construction is planned.

“You can see why that would be so interesting to an administration that wants to rush through the construction of data centers,” says Keri Powell, senior attorney and air program leader at the Southern Environmental Law Center (SELC). “What EPA would be allowing would be all of those facilities to go through and just not have to deal with the public, issue the permits in secret behind closed doors. Nobody knows what’s happening until the bulldozers are out there.”

highlights.title: ‘I wanted to find the slowest fashion imaginable’: the woman growing her own dress
highlights.summary: Looking for an alternative to fast fashion, Eve Ogden Schaub decided to create a garment from homegrown flax. From crop tops to shorts and brightly patterned dresses, many of today’s clothes are the result of fast fashion.
body: Eve Ogden Schaub is in the midst of a project to create a linen garment made from flax she is growing at home, documenting the process in videos shared on her Instagram account.
“I had this idea that I wanted to find the slowest fashion imaginable. And that’s when I had the idea I could grow a dress from seed in my back yard,” she says.

Schaub began the project in April 2025 when she turned a 600 sq ft vegetable garden in Vermont into a plot for growing flax. Having harvested the first crop, Schaub sowed and harvested a second. She is also learning to process the material in steps that would not sound amiss in a Grimms’ fairytale – sometimes enlisting family and friends to help.

“We retted it, which is a sort of decomposition process, and then you do breaking and scutching and hackling, and you have to spin and scour and then maybe dye your yarn,” she says, adding that she has yet to get to the latter step, but is growing indigo plants for the purpose.

From crop tops to shorts and brightly patterned dresses, many of today’s clothes are the result of fast fashion.

highlights.title: Musicians-turned-detectives are hunting for AI grifters
highlights.summary: As audio-focused generative tools and platforms have gotten more sophisticated, the internet has become increasingly filled with AI-generated music whose melodies and vocals are algorithmically derived from the work of human artists.
body: As AI infiltrates the electronic dance music scene, a callout culture is brewing.

For musicians — especially those creating art in technologically-focused spaces like electronic dance music — the increasingly complicated question of what is “real” and what isn’t feels particularly urgent and personal. Professional courtesy can make this only more complex; listeners can call out performers they suspect of using gen AI, but it’s something else for artists to raise concerns about their professional peers. There are some though, like 26-year-old EDM producer Max “H4RRIS” Harris, who are taking a stand against generative technology with videos calling out anyone they believe is trying to pass off AI slop as human-made art.

When I recently spoke with Harris, he told me that he sees AI-generated music as “a kind of decoy art form,” and he thinks that the people making it don’t really have anything meaningful to say with their creations. He feels that true art in any medium is “created by people that are trying to express feelings and messages,” and he believes that the only thing AI boosters are really interested in is making a quick profit.

highlights.title: AI Has Human Doctors Asking: What’s Left for Us?
highlights.summary: A recent paper argues that AI is often better at doctoring than doctors. Guess who isn't thrilled.
body: Don’t be fooled by the question mark in the title of an article published this month in the Journal of the American Medical Association. When the authors, including medical superstar Ezekiel Emanuel and venture capitalist Vinod Khosla, asked, “ Will Autonomous AI Exceed AI-Physicians as the Best Medical Care? ” they were being rhetorical. Their answer is an emphatic YES. Many in the medical world are begrudgingly coming to terms with the premise that patients can get the best treatment by a hybrid approach where doctors work in consultation with well-trained bots. But this article’s thesis is that AI alone can deliver the best outcomes.

highlights.title: GTA 6's gameplay reveal pulled in 3.97 million peak viewers, overwhelming Twitch and Netflix in the process
highlights.summary: Reaction streams to Grand Theft Auto 6 's first gameplay presentation peaked at 3,970,738 viewers across livestreaming platforms, making it the biggest gaming stream of 2026 so far.
body: That's according to new data from Streams Charts, which claims 9,038 streamers covered Rockstar Games ' Netflix reveal, racking up 5,227,798 hours watched.

That puts GTA 6's reveal ahead of Summer Game Fest 2026's 3.81 million peak viewers, as well as June's Nintendo Direct and State of Play broadcasts. Twitch carried the largest share of the audience, accounting for around 44 percent of total hours watched, ahead of YouTube (34.8% percent) and Kick (20.2 percent).
Spanish streamer Juan Alberto "IlloJuan" García led the way with 233,520 peak viewers, a new record for his own channel, ahead of Rubius (191,056) and IShowSpeed (177,887).

The reveal went out at 8pm UK time, but heavy demand caused technical issues on both Netflix and Twitch, with some viewers reportedly locked out for 40-50 minutes. That didn't deter internet hype, though; Streams Charts also tracked more than 100,000 chat messages about the game across the three-hour window it analysed.

highlights.summary: The ‘Golden girls of Eastbourne’ first crossed paths more than 50 years ago. They recall flammable feather head-dresses, wardrobe malfunctions and topping the bill over the Beatles.
body: I hear the Golden Girls of Eastbourne before I see them – hooting laughter leaking out of a house in the East Sussex seaside town. Inside, I find five energetic women in their 80s and 90s, sitting in a knick-knack-filled living room and talking over one another like teenagers.

Friends for more than half a century, the women met in rehearsals and aftershow parties while working as dancers, singers and comedy stooges in the 1960s and 70s. Their careers took them from cruise ships and panto to British seaside theatres, where they performed in sequin dresses, high-cut leotards and huge feather headdresses, sharing bills with the biggest stars of the day.
He decided to photograph them at the town’s Royal Hippodrome – a Victorian theatre where all the women performed when they were younger.

“It’s a beautiful theatre,” says former dancer and dance teacher Jenny Lawrenson, 83. Petite, with the voice of Mary Poppins and the impeccable posture of a lifelong ballet dancer, she says she remembers it better for another reason – its tilted stage: “You’re dancing uphill!”

highlights.title: Neocloud Lambda secures $1B in debt to buy more chips
highlights.summary: Neocloud Lambda has raised $1B in private debt to buy Nvidia AI chips and lease them to Microsoft. It's the latest in a string of loans, underscoring the high cost of the AI boom.
body: Lambda, an AI cloud company that buys computing chips and rents them out to businesses, has raised $1 billion in private, short-dated debt to buy Nvidia’s AI chips that it will lease to Microsoft, Bloomberg reports.

The terms of the deal, which Bloomberg says was arranged by JP Morgan Chase, signal that Lambda is betting it will be able to quickly deploy the chips and start generating revenue from them, letting it repay the debt fairly quickly using that incoming cash.

This is the latest in a string of loans that Lambda is using to fund GPU infrastructure for specific customers. In May, it closed a $1 billion secured credit facility, and this week it announced the closing of a $926 million loan to fund Nvidia GB300 GPUs, one of Nvidia’s newest chip models, for a deployment it’s under contract to provide Nvidia.

The $1 billion private debt deal comes as Lambda is reportedly in talks for a $3 billion pre-IPO round. The company last November raised $1.5 billion in venture capital at a $5.43 billion post-money valuation, per PitchBook data.

highlights.title: How 'Coyote vs. ACME' Broke All the Rules of Live-Action Looney Tunes Movies, and Got Away with It
highlights.summary: "We really wanted to challenge ourselves to not acknowledge the Looney Tunes as an ensemble of characters," director Dave Green tells Polygon.
body: When Michael Jordan first meets Bugs Bunny in Space Jam, he reacts with star-studded confusion, which is probably how any human being would react to meeting the iconic cartoon rabbit in real life. But when Will Forte meets the beloved Looney Tune in Coyote vs. ACME, he's surprisingly nonplussed. That's because, in the new live-action/animated feature film, the Looney Tunes aren't global icons, they're just regular (cartoon) people living in our world.
Foghorn is a blowhard who has a lot of swagger and arrogance and likes to talk down to people.

Unlike Space Jam and Looney Tunes: Back in Action — or even Who Framed Roger Rabbit — the Looney Tunes characters are not celebrities in Coyote vs. ACME. In those other movies, the Looney Tunes characters play famous versions of themselves that had starred in all those animated shorts from back in the day, but in Coyote vs. ACME, they’re just regular people living in a world populated by both humans and cartoon characters. In that sense, Coyote vs. ACME operates more like a movie-length Looney Tunes animated short than a live-action movie with Looney Tunes characters in it.

highlights.title: An Anthropic researcher just gave us a peek at self-improving AI
highlights.summary: Given 10 benchmarks for specific misaligned behaviors, the automated systems were able to improve performance on every single one without degrading overall performance.
body: Training AI models with other AI models has become a very popular goal for neolabs — and now, a researcher in Anthropic’s fellows program has given us an early look at what it might look like in practice.

Led by Anthropic fellow Chen Yueh-Han, the system replicates much of the traditional approach to research. Each automated system searches the available literature, proposes a method, and trains the model using that method for 30 minutes, gradually increasing the benchmark over several iterations. Effective methods are preserved while ineffective ones are discarded, allowing the system to operate quickly and at a great scale.
“Overall, these results provide early evidence that automated alignment post-training could become practical in the near term,” the paper reads.

The paper is a step toward recursive self-improvement, which many see as the next significant step in AI progress. If models can improve their own alignment training, it’s plausible they could improve training practices more broadly — at which point, human AI researchers might soon become obsolete.

highlights.title: Gamescom Responds To Rampant Reports Of Theft At The Event
highlights.summary: Theft has become a major problem at Gamescom 2026, with at least three indie studios speaking out about the equipment stolen from their event booths. The organization behind the event has acknowledged this matter in an underwhelming X post that did not indicate it would provide indie exhibitors…
body: Reports of theft first emerged when Mimic solo developer Ryan Laley reported that their laptop and other equipment in the expo area near him were stolen. According to Ryan Laley's video explaining the ordeal, the hardware was snatched overnight from an area that is supposed to have restricted access overnight and be monitored by the security team at all times.

In the same raid, Tessera Studios, which was showcasing the game The Zibbo Show, lost personal computers, two laptops, and a Steam Deck, all containing game demos and confidential company information. Additionally, two computers were stolen from indie game publisher iam8bit Presents' booth, risking leaks of its games, Petal Runner and Escape Academy 2.

Ukiyo Studios then chimed in to recall that one of its laptops was taken from a Gamescom booth two years ago. It claims that when it tried to report the theft, event personnel attempted to stop Ukiyo so it wouldn't taint Gamescom and the city of Cologne's public image. Furthermore, Ukiyo says that despite attending dozens of events every year, Gamescom is the only one where it makes sure to lock up the equipment overnight due to inadequate security measures.
